755 allows owner to write while others can only read/execute. 777 lets anyone modify your files.

patterns.tip: Double-check device with lsblk before running
patterns.explain: Always run lsblk to confirm which /dev/sdX is your intended target. One letter off wipes the wrong disk.

patterns.tip: Do a dry-run first with -n flag
patterns.explain: Add --dry-run to rsync to preview exactly which files would be deleted at the destination.
--force-with-lease only force pushes if no one else has pushed since your last fetch — much safer.

patterns.safer:
git stash   # save work first
# then: git reset --hard
patterns.explain: git stash saves your current changes before the reset so you can recover them with git stash pop.

patterns.safer: git clean -n   # dry-run: shows what would be deleted
patterns.explain: git clean -n lists all files that would be removed without actually deleting anything.
Saves your entire crontab to a backup file before deleting it. Restore with: crontab ~/crontab.backup
terraform plan -destroy shows exactly what would be destroyed before you commit to it.
Export all resources to YAML before deletion so you have a record. Namespace deletion is permanent.

patterns.tip: Preview what would be removed first
patterns.safer: docker system df   # shows what would be freed
patterns.explain: docker system df shows the space used by images, containers, and volumes that prune would delete.
sed -i.bak creates a .bak backup of the original file before modifying it in place.

patterns.tip: Verify the target path carefully — this is permanent
patterns.explain: shred overwrites data multiple times making recovery impossible. Confirm the exact file path first.

patterns.safer: lsblk -f   # shows all devices with filesystem labels
patterns.explain: lsblk -f shows device names, sizes, and existing filesystems. Make absolutely sure you have the right device.

patterns.tip: Back up the user home directory first
patterns.explain: Create a tarball of the user home directory before deletion.
Saves your firewall rules before flushing. Restore with: iptables-restore < /tmp/iptables.backup
